description.narrative:
Since the Russian Federation’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Ukraine has faced a severe humanitarian crisis marked by widespread death and displacement, over USD 152 billion in direct damage, and major setbacks to progress on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Women are disproportionately affected by Russia’s systematic attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including health, education, and energy services. Their rights are violated daily, while accountability remains limited. Women make up the majority of refugees, returnees, and internally displaced persons. At the same time, the needs of women and girls continue to grow as financial and human resources become increasingly strained. During 2025–2029, UN Women Ukraine will work to ensure that women and men, girls and boys, and their communities benefit from gender-responsive recovery, sustainable development, transitional justice, and humanitarian assistance that protects access to rights and essential services. Guided by its triple mandate, context analysis, lessons learned, and comparative advantages, UN Women will advance gender equality and women’s empowerment across the Humanitarian–Development–Peace (HDP) nexus.
The Strategic Note contributes to two outcomes of the UN Cooperation Framework 2025–2029, five UN Women Strategic Plan outcomes, and at least six global gender equality accelerators.
The Strategic Note is informed by consultations with national and regional government partners, the private sector, women’s rights organizations, UN entities, donors, and development partners, as well as ongoing engagement with women’s groups facing multiple forms of discrimination.
Norway will support the implementation of UN Women Ukraine’s Strategic Note through a two-year agreement.
